findings.evidence: The alert-feed path is fully independent of the kill-switch. alertCache.refresh() (packages/web-server/src/services/alertCache.ts:127-128) fetches directly from ATHENA_HUNTER_URL ('http://athena-hunter:8005', line 3) via `${ATHENA_HUNTER_URL}/alerts/recent`, never routing through the orchestrator. The web-server broadcast loop (packages/web-server/src/index.ts:121-138 trickleNext -> alertCache.dequeue) pushes those alerts over the WS 'alert_feed' channel, and /api/v1/alerts/recent (packages/web-server/src/api/chat.ts:133-136) serves alertCache.recentEmitted(20). The kill-switch is an in-memory dict in a DIFFERENT process: agents/orchestrator/main.py:673 `_kill_switches: dict[str, bool] = {"athena_hunter": False}`, flipped at main.py:698-703, and consulted ONLY on the /query intent path (main.py:841 `if _kill_switches.get("athena_hunter")`). alertCache.ts contains zero references to any kill-switch, orchestrator URL, or admin state. Live confirmation: GET https://aing.bhnoc.com/api/v1/alerts/recent returned 20 live Athena-derived alerts (real conference IPs 192.168.128-131.x, 10.220.x, timestamps 2026-07-24 ~02:xx) with no gating. Impact: after an operator hits the emergency stop, interactive chat serves the cover response but the sidebar keeps broadcasting real Athena alerts (IPs, cert/DNS/UA detections) to every connected client and the REST endpoint. This is the exact opposite of what 'kill athena' promises, so it is a real security/operational gap, not cosmetic.
findings.fix: Have the feed consult the same kill state. Minimal: web-server polls the orchestrator's GET /admin/killswitch (already exists, main.py:692) on a short interval, and short-circuit both trickleNext (skip dequeue/broadcast) and /api/v1/alerts/recent to return [] when athena_hunter is killed. Alternatively gate athena-hunter's own /alerts/recent behind the same switch so the source stops serving. Do NOT rely on the orchestrator's in-memory dict alone — it must be reachable from the web-server process (shared store or the admin GET).

findings.evidence: SAME UNDERLYING BUG AS cc-2 (see note). alertCache.dequeue() (alertCache.ts:87-108) masks restricted subnets on srcIp/dstIp via maskIp->scrubString (lines 91-96) and on description via scrubString (line 102), but copies the composite id verbatim: line 98 `id: raw.id`. scrubString (lines 19-28) is never applied to id. The id is built upstream as `alert_name|orig_h|ts`. Live proof: GET https://aing.bhnoc.com/api/v1/alerts/recent returned an alert with `"id":"File Hosting Service Domain Domain in DNS Lookup (files .pythonhosted .org)|10.220.199.121|2026-07-24 02:59:47"` while the SAME record's `"srcIp":"10.220.69.121"` was masked (octet 199 -> decoy 69). Octet 199 is in RESTRICTED_OCTETS (line 14). This id reaches the DOM (data-id) and the raw JSON, leaking the true restricted-subnet host that was deliberately masked everywhere else. (Note: this snapshot did not contain the hunter's exact .153.11 example, and one alert had `10.220.198.30` in its id — octet 198 is NOT restricted, so that one is legitimately unmasked and is not evidence.)
findings.fix: Run the id through the same scrubber before emitting: in dequeue(), set `id: scrubString(raw.id) ?? raw.id` (line 98). scrubString already handles the pipe-delimited IP in-place. Keep timestamps/names untouched — only the embedded 10.220.<restricted> octet is rewritten to the .69 decoy, matching srcIp behavior. Verify id uniqueness is preserved (multiple restricted hosts collapsing to .69 is acceptable given ts is part of the key).

findings.evidence: DUPLICATE of lo-1 — same root cause: alertCache.ts:98 `id: raw.id` bypasses the scrubString sanitizer that is applied to srcIp/dstIp/description (lines 91-102). Restricted octets in RESTRICTED_OCTETS={12,13,14,15,150,152,153,154,199} (line 14) leak raw in the id string. Live evidence identical to lo-1: `"id":"...|10.220.199.121|2026-07-24 02:59:47"` with masked `"srcIp":"10.220.69.121"` from https://aing.bhnoc.com/api/v1/alerts/recent. lo-1 and cc-2 are the SAME bug and should be tracked as one.
findings.fix: Same single fix as lo-1: apply scrubString to raw.id at alertCache.ts:98. One-line change resolves both lo-1 and cc-2.
